    formal management guidance
    conditions
    We expect first quarter 2025 total revenue to be in the range of $39.5-41.8 billion. This reflects 8-15% year-over-year growth, or 11-18% growth on a constant currency basis as our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 3% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates. This also reflects the effect of lapping leap day in the first quarter of 2024. While we are not providing a full year 2025 revenue outlook, we expect the investments we are making in our core business this year will give us an opportunity to continue delivering strong revenue growth throughout 2025.

This reflects 8-15% year-over-year growth, or 11-18% growth on a constant currency basis as our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 3% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates. interpretation
Consistently conservative near-term revenue guidance is useful but does not establish multi-year AI returns. Capex forecasts have been repeatedly revised upward; investment cost visibility is weaker than revenue range delivery. Do not convert beat frequency into an automatic valuation multiplier.
limitations
limitations · 3 records
  1. No all-ever statement audit. Sample starts Q 3 2023, excluding earlier pandemic/advertising-cycle stress.
  2. Exact original quarterly reported values retained; FY 2026 Q 2 YTD total differs by USD 1 m from addition of separately released Q 1/Q 2, likely rounding/recast unresolved.
  3. Changes in CFO responsibility and team execution preclude attributing all outcomes solely to CEO.

    rationale
    Ad monetization slows while fixed AI capacity and Reality Labs costs persist. Three-year annual net-reinvestment floors prevent a low-growth scenario from erasing committed spending.
    valuation Status
    Illustrative operating value only. Equity bridge, timing and model gaps unresolved; not a price target.
    simple Terminal Sales Capital From ROIC
    0.5
    terminal Capital Convention
    Explicit reinvestment uses delta revenue / S:C. Terminal reinvestment uses next-year NOPAT × g / ROIC. Therefore the matching incremental S:C is ROIC / [(1+g) × terminal margin × (1-tax)], rather than the simplified ROIC / after-tax margin ratio. Both are disclosed.

    capital Path Rationale
    Keep the stated early investment intensity, then apply the disclosed normalization path where present. Fade the final years to terminal-ROIC-consistent incremental capital efficiency so reinvestment and FCFF do not jump at the terminal boundary. This path is analytical, not company spending guidance.
    implementation Status
    Requires the explicit annual reinvestment path and any spending floors; do not substitute one fixed S:C input.

model Gaps
model Gaps · 6 records
  1. Revenue-based reinvestment alone cannot represent multi-year firm capacity obligations, construction-in-progress, replacement cycles or early low utilization. Bear includes explicit net investment floors not currently expressible by a single S:C input.
  2. Margin ramp is illustrative linear five-year convergence, not a contract-level depreciation/expense model.
  3. Legal accounting expense and cash settlement timing differ. Current engine other Claims can carry an assumed PV but cannot infer the payment schedule or approval probability.
  4. TTM financial baseline June 2026 is not an October balance-sheet roll-forward; pending Q 3 results cannot be invented.
  5. Base first3years now use direct capital/D&A/WC inputs; derived S:C is descriptive. Cash-funding view adds back noncash SBC separately from economic FCFF. Interest, legal/claims, lease credit and reserve schedules remain to be integrated.
  6. Base first3years now use direct capital/D&A/WC inputs; derived S:C is descriptive. Cash-funding view adds back noncash SBC separately from economic FCFF. Interest, legal/claims, lease credit and reserve schedules remain to be integrated.
confidence
confidence · 4 fields
near Term Revenue
medium-high supported by formal guide and 12 quarter conservative sample
long Run Revenue
medium-low
capital Intensity
low-medium: very large multiyear commitments
claims Bridge
incomplete
invalidation
invalidation · 4 records
  1. Advertising growth falls below 10% for several comparable quarters without FX explanation.
  2. AI capex does not produce engagement/monetization or excess capacity becomes visible.
  3. Normalized consolidated margin stays below 30% despite scaling, or annual net reinvestment remains above modeled levels.
  4. State settlement, other litigation or venture support crystallizes beyond modeled scenarios.
not Used
not Used · 3 records
  1. Share-price calibration
  2. Unverified consensus
  3. Automatic CEO credibility premium
forecast Basis
Annual rolling periods after the June 2026 TTM anchor: year one ends approximately June 2027. Calendar-2026 management guidance is a near-term reference, not mechanically the same forecast period. Post-quarter claims require a separate valuation-date bridge.
terminal Transition Policy
Final explicit S:C reconciles to forward-NOPAT terminal reinvestment. Stable growth, tax, margin and ROIC remain unchanged; terminal FCFF grows at stable g from the final explicit FCFF.
duration Sensitivity Definition
Six constant-S:C duration diagnostics, preserving the initial ratio-based model to isolate duration. They do not include the final capital-efficiency transition in the selected base, so the 3/10 diagnostic is not identical to the selected base valuation.

    rationale
    Sustained ad improvements, messaging monetization and commercially successful new AI services; capacity becomes more efficient and Reality Labs losses shrink as a revenue share. Five high-growth years and 15-year fade require new-market proof.
    valuation Status
    Illustrative operating value only. Equity bridge, timing and model gaps unresolved; not a price target.
    simple Terminal Sales Capital From ROIC
    0.4999999999999999
    terminal Capital Convention
    Explicit reinvestment uses delta revenue / S:C. Terminal reinvestment uses next-year NOPAT × g / ROIC. Therefore the matching incremental S:C is ROIC / [(1+g) × terminal margin × (1-tax)], rather than the simplified ROIC / after-tax margin ratio. Both are disclosed.
    terminal Capital Fade Begins After Year
    10
    terminal Capital Fade Ends Year
    15
    incremental Sales To Capital Early
    0.7
    terminal FCFF
    360873.273288021
    terminal FCFFGrowth From Final Explicit Year
    0.02499999999999858
    capital Path Rationale
    Keep the stated early investment intensity, then apply the disclosed normalization path where present. Fade the final years to terminal-ROIC-consistent incremental capital efficiency so reinvestment and FCFF do not jump at the terminal boundary. This path is analytical, not company spending guidance.
    implementation Status
    Requires the explicit annual reinvestment path and any spending floors; do not substitute one fixed S:C input.

bounded Model Gaps
bounded Model Gaps · 8 records
  1. Valuation-date stub and post-anchor cash/claims/share roll-forward not integrated; this is a forecast-origin operating EV, not October 17 equity value.
  2. No probability weighting or share-price calibration. Source forecast assumptions are judgments, not reported facts.
  3. Enterprise-to-equity bridge is not computed here; consult the company-specific claim register for resolved evidence, assumptions and remaining uncertainties. Zero is not evidence of absence.
  4. Cash capital-spend guidance is not identical to economic additions; separately reconcile supplier payable changes, lease capitalization and asset commissioning.
  5. Depreciation ramps with in-service timing, useful lives and hardware replacement, not merely spending date.
  6. Cash taxes versus normalized operating taxes, interest and nonoperating income require a cash waterfall.
  7. SBC must either remain an economic expense with consistent future share treatment, or be modeled through awards/dilution consistently; no double count.
  8. A lower cash deficit does not prove attractive incremental returns.

method
Start with source-anchored timing of cash capital expenditures, subtract modeled economic D&A, add core operating WC, and retain SBC in EBIT for economic FCFF. Add assumed noncash SBC only in a separate cash-funding view, then subtract separately modeled employee share-settlement cash. The 60% Meta settlement ratio is an assumption, not a repeated historical law. Actual OCF contains tax/nonoperating/working-capital timing and is not normalized FCFF.
assumptions
2026H2 capex is derived from formal guide minus actualH1. For next rolling year, illustrative2027H1 spending is80% of lowH2,90% of midpointH2,or120% of highH2. Years2–3 capex, D&A and WC are analyst scenarios, not a2027/2028 management guide.

remaining Gates · 5 records
  1. Cash capital-spend guidance is not identical to economic additions; separately reconcile supplier payable changes, lease capitalization and asset commissioning.
  2. Depreciation ramps with in-service timing, useful lives and hardware replacement, not merely spending date.
  3. Cash taxes versus normalized operating taxes, interest and nonoperating income require a cash waterfall.
  4. SBC must either remain an economic expense with consistent future share treatment, or be modeled through awards/dilution consistently; no double count.
  5. A lower cash deficit does not prove attractive incremental returns.
